candidates.story: On November 6, 2026, Elon Musk announced Tesla will end Cybertruck production in mid-2027 — the truck was designed with installed capacity for 250,000 units per year but has sold roughly 12% of that target, a failure that began at the 2019 unveiling when Musk's 'armor glass' window shattered live on stage during the demo.
candidates.why_funny: The truck built to withstand anything immediately couldn't survive a metal ball thrown by its own designer, and seven years later it also couldn't survive the market.
candidates.alt: Cracked Tesla Cybertruck 'armor glass' window at the November 2019 unveiling event, with fracture lines radiating from the steel-ball impact point across the dark glass pane

candidates.tagline: A ring with a screen, joystick, and mic — for when your phone is too convenient.
candidates.story: On November 5, 2026, hardware startup Aina launched the Aina Ring — a $399–$499 titanium ring with a small screen, joystick, microphone, and speaker to control AI agents — whose standout use case in the first review was acting as an Apple TV remote when the reviewer couldn't find the actual Apple TV remote.
candidates.why_funny: Aina built a $400 AI-powered finger computer to solve the problem of needing to look at your phone, and the clearest real-world win was replacing a device that costs $19.
candidates.alt: The Aina AI Ring product, a chunky titanium band with a small rectangular screen and a joystick nub visible on its flat top surface, shown in a product photograph
